title: Benny Daniels, and "Toledo Shout" with Addison
summary: Singer Benny Daniels's reception, and Ramirez and Addison playing "The Toledo Shout" which Addison had done with Art Tatum in Toledo.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And that was on the north side of 52nd Street. So there was a big thing about later on, where they... Benny Daniels sang "Tout Suite"(?), he used to sing "My Diane," and he

looked like a White boy, so that didn't go over too well. They liked him. The women loved it, but the men didn't...I mean, they abhorred it! So what are you gonna do? And that's with Bernard Addison. We played things like "The Toledo Shout." And I apologized to him, because he used to do that with Art Tatum when they were back in Toledo, you know.
Oh, I didn't know Bernard Addison worked with Art Tatum.
Oh yeah, in Toledo, Ohio. They did "The Toledo Shout," and they released(?) it. He came up with Art Tatum.
